checks.claim: BT1 Cameron-Martin identification: L=sqrt(delta)K, ker L=H_seen^perp, H_CM=L(H_seen), ||Lh||_CM=||P_seen h||, CM unit ball = sqrt(delta)K(Ball_H(1))
checks.reason: The closed first chaos of X is the closure of the span of W(k_l), which is W(H_seen), so H_mu={E[X W(h)]:h in H_seen} with norm ||h||. P_seen maps Ball_H(r) onto Ball_{H_seen}(r) and L kills H_seen^perp, so L(Ball_H(1)) is the closed CM unit ball and K(Ball_H(r)) equals the seen-ball image. Unused directions are handled correctly.

checks.claim: BT1 geometry: K(Ball_H(r)) is compact, T_r=A+K(Ball_H(r)) is closed/Borel, {D<=r}=T_r, D is Borel and finite a.s.
checks.reason: Closed Hilbert balls are weakly compact and compact K maps weakly convergent sequences to norm-convergent ones, so the image is compact. A is closed, and closed plus compact is closed. Attainment: if x is in T_s for every s>r, write x=a_n+K phi_n with ||phi_n||<=r+1/n. A weakly convergent subsequence has a limit phi with ||phi||<=r, K phi_n -> K phi, and a_n -> x-K phi lies in A because A is closed. Hence {D<=r}=T_r is closed, D is lower semicontinuous and therefore Borel, and P(D(X)>r)=mu(T_r^c)->0. This needs only fixed-delta compactness. The Friz-Hairer outer-measure footnote is avoided because the sets are closed.

T_r=A+(r/sqrt(delta))𝒦 exactly, so the source CM radius is r/sqrt(delta), not r and not sqrt(delta)r. Markov gives P(||X||>b)<=1/2, so hat a>=0, and barPhi is decreasing with barPhi(y)<=exp(-y^2/2) for y>=0, as on printed p.190. Theorem 11.6 (both page images checked against the excerpt) requires an AWS and a Borel A with mu(A)>0, and both hold when b>0. The v2 tail rows check actual <= Borell <= Rayleigh on exact 1-D laws.

checks.claim: BT1b: radial Rayleigh expectation bound with nondecreasing, possibly jumping G; no selector, no density, zero law without F(0)=0
checks.reason: Attainment gives F(X)<=G(D(X)) a.s. with no measurable control selector. For phi=exp(G/delta)>=0 nondecreasing, the level sets {phi>t} are half-lines [c,inf) or (c,inf). P(D>=c) is the left limit of P(D>r) for r below c, which is at most P(R>=c)=P(R>c) because the Rayleigh law is continuous, so the layer-cake comparison survives jumps of G. The Rayleigh density (r/delta)exp(-r^2/(2delta)) gives the stated integral, with an infinite right side allowed. Zero law: exp(G(0)/delta) is at most the integral because G is nondecreasing and the Rayleigh mass is 1. F(0)=0 is not needed. No finite-dimensional density is used.

minor: The scalar 'tube bound >= true MGF' assertion in check-gaussian-tubes-v1/v2 is tautological for linear F. The gap is |p|b + delta log j, and j = ∫_0^∞ u exp(-(u-t)^2/2) du >= 1 for every t >= 0 (j=1 at t=0 and j'(t)=sqrt(2π)Phi(t)>0), so it cannot fail. Only the wrong-CM and doubled-action rows and the actual<=Borell<=Rayleigh tail rows carry falsification content. falsification-v1 does not label this.

The diagnostic counts overstate independent evidence. p=-1 and p=+1 moment rows are identical by symmetry, p=0 and lambda=0 rows are zero signals, and the nonzero tail rows do not depend on lambda (the lambda=0.5 and lambda=2 rows are identical). That leaves about 8 distinct nontrivial moment cases and 16 distinct nonzero tail cases.

Notation overloads should be disambiguated in the proof: L (covariance sqrt(delta)K vs horizon 1/delta), A (base ball vs BT3a intercept), B (Banach space vs block integer), C_B (primitive constant vs BT2c constant), K (compact operator vs CM unit ball 𝒦), and a_m (residual block norms in finite-reuse JSON vs GL/C3 mean budgets).

BT2c's 'uniformly R>=1, delta small' would read better as 'with a constant independent of delta and of R (R=1/delta+2), for all 0<delta<min(1,1/B)'. 'Delta small' is not needed for the envelope itself.

BT2 should state explicitly that SA's auxiliary exponents (theta<eta_time<beta_time, fixed even Q with Q gamma>d, beta_time-eta_time-1/Q>0, Q>2d/(1-a)) are chosen compatibly with BT2's theta. Only the crosswalk mentions the fixed even Q.
The cell-diagnostic text writes the upper scale as sqrt(delta log n)+delta/sqrt(delta log n), but the script uses log(2n). This is cosmetic and the bound is valid.
